text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - Tunisia bought two lots of U.S.-origin corn of 25,000 tonnes each at a tender on Wednesday, traders said. The first lot was bought at $141.45 C&F for January 1-10 shipment, and the second at $141.75 for shipment January 20-31.

BARLEY SALE - Saudi Arabia bought 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin feed barley at a tender at prices ranging from $154 to $156 per tonne, including cost and freight, European grain traders said. The barley is for delivery up to January 31, they said.
WHEAT SALE - Sri Lanka bought on Tuesday night a total of 100,000 tonnes of Australian and Argentinian wheat, U.S. exporters said.

VEGOIL SALE - Egypt bought 35,000 tonnes of vegetable oil on Wednesday for delivery in the first half of January, an official from the state Holding Company for Food Industries said. The breakdown includes 25,000 tonnes +/- five percent of sunflower oil at $537 C+F from Alexandria from Topfer International and 10,000 tonnes +/- five percent of palm oil at $546.75 C+F from Alexandria from Felda International of Malaysia.

SOYBEAN SALE - Egypt has bought 30,000 tonnes of soybean from the Swiss company Romak for $296 C&F per tonne for delivery in the first half of December, an official from the state Holding Company for Food Industries said on Wednesday. Head of Sales Muharram Ghanem said that the shipment had a buyer's option of plus or minus five percent.
VEGOIL TENDERS - Pakistani traders said on Wednesday the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) issued a tender for the supply of 6,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil for shipment up to December 31.

WHEAT TENDERS - Moroccan millers will tender on November 28 to import 20,000 tonnes of Argentine soft wheat for December 20-30 delivery, European grain traders said. The tender will be held by the Association Professionnelle de la Minoterie.

- Pakistan issued separate tenders on Saturday for 225,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat and Australian white milling wheat for delivery between December 11 and 31, the Food and Agriculture Ministry said. The ministry invited bids on December 1.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - Bangladesh has tendered for 200,000 tonnes of U.S. grade-2 wheat for shipment in January and February, food ministry officials said. They said the ministry would receive offers until 0600 GMT on November 30. The shipment for the first 100,000 tonnes should be completed by January 10 and the rest by February 10. The results of the bids will not be known until Dec 3.

- Algeria is expected this Friday to seek 100,000 tonnes optional origin wheat which would include French, U.S. or Argentine wheat, U.S. exporters said. Shipment was slated for last-half Dec. The class of wheat was not given, they said.

BARLEY TENDER - Cyprus on Wednesday invited tenders for the supply of 25,000 tonnes feed barley with a shipment date December 1996 or January 1997. Tenders close on December 3, a statement from the Cyprus Grain Commission said.

LENTIL TENDER - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 9,500 tonnes of lentils for export. December 16 was set as final date for bids and results would be announced on December 17.
MARKET TALK - Turkish and U.S. officials said on Wednesday a dispute between the two countries over Turkey's crackdown on imported wheat from the United States had practically ended.
